N° 06A French saga, an essay and an encyclopedia2026

How to use 1884

For French-speaking readers who want a long, hard novel about power in Africa, students and teachers looking for the history behind it, and anyone who wants to understand the methods of a regime before reading the news.

Open 1884 ↗Platform detailsContact

Guided tourReal screens

Plays automatically. Use the dots or arrows to move, Pause to stop.

01

Getting started

1

Go to saga-1884.vercel.app.

2

Read the essay on the home page, or jump to one of the seven words.

3

Open La saga and start with the prologue, Le pays signé.

4

Use Suivant at the bottom of each chapter; the site remembers where you stopped.

5

Open Encyclopédie when you lose track of a name, a place or a word.

02

Features

01

The diagnosis

The home page names the problem without politeness, in seven parts that follow one argument, from the philosophy we lost to the DNA that holds the answer.

STEPS

  1. Scroll from the hero
  2. Pick one of the seven words
  3. Read to Commencer la lecture
02

Adinkra and the cloth

Six adinkra symbols with their meanings, drawn by hand in code, and behind the text a cloth that changes for each part: ndop, kente, bogolan, Kuba raffia, Ndebele walls.

STEPS

  1. Open Philosophie
  2. Read each symbol's meaning
  3. Watch the cloth change as you scroll
03

History drawn in code

The Ishango bone with its groups of 11, 13, 17 and 19 notches, the silhouettes of Giza, Aksum, Great Zimbabwe, Djenné and Lalibela, and a timeline of the revolution era from 1948 to 1991.

STEPS

  1. Open Histoire
  2. Read the roots, the kingdoms and the wound
  3. Follow the timeline of independences
04

Black face, white mask

A mask cut in two, dark and white, for the part on mimicry: the skin creams, the forbidden mother tongues, the copied constitutions and the elite that kept the colonial state as it was.

STEPS

  1. Open Le masque
  2. Read on to La politique qui a échoué
05

The reader

One chapter at a time on a paper page, with a larger or smaller text and a night page. Each chapter has its own address you can share.

STEPS

  1. Open La saga
  2. Use A+ or A- for the text size
  3. Press Nuit for a dark page
  4. Press Suivant to go on
06

The table of contents

Five books, fifty chapters and five memories of real history, with a dot on every chapter already read.

STEPS

  1. On a phone, press Sommaire
  2. Pick any chapter
  3. Look for the gold dots to see what you read
07

Encyclopedia

125 entries in a dictionary layout: characters, institutions of the regime, places, rituals, objects and words of the country. Search any name, filter by kind, and links open the chapters where it matters.

STEPS

  1. Open Encyclopédie
  2. Type a name in the search
  3. Tick Montrer les révélations only after the end
08

A railway from 1884 to 2035

A 3D railway with 34 milestones: pale ones for the real history of Cameroon, gold ones for the events of the novel. Each opens a card with the chapter to read.

STEPS

  1. Open Chronologie 3D
  2. Drag the year slider
  3. Touch a milestone
09

Cameroon in relief

The real map of Cameroon in 3D, dressed in ndop, with twelve pins where the novel takes place, from Douala and Yaoundé to Bafang, Buea and Maroua.

STEPS

  1. Open Carte 3D
  2. Drag to turn the map
  3. Touch a pin to read its story
10

The Theory and the Manual

The regime's fourteen rules of quiet domination face the people's fourteen answers, rule against rule, from never appearing to writing the contract.

STEPS

  1. Open La Théorie et le Manuel
  2. Read each rule with its answer
03Tips
  • Read the essay first: it gives the seven ideas the novel turns into scenes.
  • Keep the encyclopedia open in another tab; the spoilers stay hidden until you ask for them.
  • The memories of 1914, 1958, 1971, 1991 and 2016 follow real history; the chapters around them are fiction.
04FAQ
Is it a true story?

The country, its cities and its history are real. The regime, its leaders and every character are invented, and no real living person or party appears.

Is it free?

Yes, every chapter is free to read online.

Is it violent?

It is hard: crude talk among the powerful, prisons, a massacre, the worst of people in every camp. Sexual violence is never shown and children are never tortured on the page, and the revolution is won without a shot fired by the people.

Can I download it?

Not for now; it reads online, chapter by chapter.
